news.title: CAF Backs Africa’s World Cup Ambitions With Bigger Investment – Motsepe
news.lede: Patrice Motsepe told the CAF Strategy Conference that the money is now flowing into African football, and that the continent will be judged on what it does with it. Motsepe said the annual grant paid to each of CAF’s 54 Member Associations has grown from R2 million to R12 million in four years. The increase gives federations more room to invest in infrastructure, coaching, competitions and administration. CAF now sets aside R900 million annually for club football, up from R300 million.

news.title: Ex-FCTA Spokesman Urges FIFA To Introduce Over-40 World Cup
news.lede: Former Spokesman of the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA), Nosike Ogbuenyi, has urged the World Football Governing body (FIFA) to introduce an Over-40 World Cup for retired football stars. Ogbuenyi made the call in Abuja after submitting a proposal for the competition to FIFA through the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) secretariat. He said the proposed tournament would enable football fans worldwide to continue enjoying the skills of legendary players beyond their active careers. He added that “the introduction of FIFA Over-40 World Cup will make the football-loving world to continue to watch the best of all time on the field of play for a longer period.”

news.title: Cruel ‘reality check’ key for Tillies stars to elevate World Cup auditions
news.lede: A cruel “reality check” from Germany could be the awakening the Matildas need heading into the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, according to Craig Foster. Joe Montemurro needed little time to see the weaknesses in his team’s tactics, as Australia’s beloved national team suffered a 4-2 loss to Germany on Saturday. Germany celebrate after their fourth goal against the Matildas. Germany needed half an hour to find the back of the net twice, with countless chances presented before those two goals also.

news.title: Wales forward Elise Hughes focused on Albania play-off before World Cup dream
news.lede: Elise Hughes has played for Charlton Athletic and Crystal Palace. Wales forward Elise Hughes says the prospect of reaching the World Cup would fulfil a lifelong ambition but insists the focus remains on Tuesday's play-off second leg against Albania. Rhian Wilkinson's side take a slender 1-0 advantage into the return fixture in Llanelli after edging the first leg of their play-off semi-final. A draw would be enough to send Wales through to the next stage of qualifying for next summer's tournament in Brazil.

news.title: He played at the World Cup after QPR, Cardiff City spells - he’s now clubless at 36
news.lede: At one stage, Junior Hoilett was one of the more exciting young attackers coming through in the Premier League but the 36-year-old has seen his career fade and he is now clubless. Junior Hoilett has had ups and downs in his career but when on the cup he was a sought-after prospect in the top-flight and seemed as though he could go on to have a sustained period in the Premier League. His career has since seen him move through the EFL and all the way down to League Two, up to Scotland, across to Germany and play in Canada, as well as playing at a FIFA World Cup. Now, though, the Ontario-born attacker finds himself without a club and looking as though his career may have come to a more abrupt end than he would have anticipated.

news.title: Two-time Rugby World Cup winner passes away, leaving rugby fans in mourning
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark Briefly News as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Cheryl Waaka, a former Black Ferns player and two-time Rugby World Cup champion, has passed away after battling stage four bowel cancer. Her whānau announced her death on Sunday, honouring her as a "beloved sister, friend and legend" whose influence stretched far beyond her playing career. Over 20 test appearances for the Black Ferns, Waaka won 19 matches and was part of the New Zealand squads that claimed World Cup titles in 1998 and 2002.

news.title: Lionel Messi Names 10 Future Stars of Football - Includes Two England Wonderkids
news.lede: Lionel Messi has bid farewell to international football and he's now given a list of youngsters he is tipping to make names for themselves on the world stage just like he did. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winning forward played his final match for Argentina last week when he captained his nation in a 3-0 friendly win over Benin. He scored from the penalty spot to end his international career with 126 goals in 208 games, of which seven of those fired his country to World Cup glory in 2022. After winning the World Cup, Messi had accomplished everything in football and realised his dream as a young boy from Rosario.
